newsitem.title: INDIA: Tibet government-in-exile fears Chinese crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Tibet government-in-exile fears Chinese crackdown.

text.p: Tibet's government-in-exile said on Monday it feared China would use last week's bomb blast in Lhasa as an excuse to increase repression in their Himalayan homeland.

"We are concerned that the Chinese authorities may use the latest incident of (a) bomb blast in Lhasa as a pretext for increasing political repression in Tibet," a statement by the exiled government, headquartered in India's Himalayan foothills, said.

"We would like to categorically point out that Dharamsala has absolutely nothing to do with this bomb blast or all the previous blasts which the Chinese authorities have accused us of," Kalon Tashi Wangdi, the government's information minister, said in the statement.
Tibet's spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, has been based in Dharamsala in the northern state of Himachal Pradesh since he fled to India in 1959 following a failed anti-Chinese uprising.
China has launched a manhunt across the restive region of Tibet after a bomb blast on Christmas Day outside government offices in the Tibetan capital of Lhasa.
Chinese officials said there was little doubt the blast was politically motivated and carried out by followers of the Dalai Lama.
